test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 29 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: The Khilafat Movement started in India _________ .

options.text: to defend the Islamic caliphate in Turkey
to oppose the massacre at Jallianwala Bagh
to oppose the restrictions upon freedom of press

solution:
The correct answer is __**to defend the Islamic caliphate in Turkey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was initiated by Indian Muslims to protest against the dismemberment of the Ottoman Empire and the abolition of the Caliphate by the British after World War I.
 
• The movement sought to preserve the authority and sanctity of the Caliph, considered the spiritual head of the global Islamic community.
 
• Key leaders of the movement included Maulana Mohammad Ali and Maulana Shaukat Ali, who were collectively known as the Ali Brothers.
 
• It was supported by Mahatma Gandhi as part of his strategy to unite Hindus and Muslims in the struggle for India's independence.
 
• The Khilafat Movement eventually declined after Mustafa Kemal Atatürk abolished the Caliphate in 1924 and established a secular government in Turkey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ottoman Empire:**

 
 
• The Ottoman Empire was a major Islamic empire that lasted from 1299 to 1922, spanning parts of Europe, Asia, and Africa.
 
• It was ruled by sultans, with the Caliph considered the religious leader of the Muslim world.
 
 
 
• **Caliphate:**
 
 
• The Caliphate refers to a form of Islamic governance led by a Caliph, who is seen as the successor to Prophet Muhammad.
 
• The Ottoman Sultan held the title of Caliph until the abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in 1924.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**
 
 
• The Khilafat Movement was closely linked to the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi, which aimed to resist British rule through nonviolent means.
 
• The two movements created a brief period of Hindu-Muslim unity in India's struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Movement:**
 
 
• Although the Khilafat Movement failed to achieve its goals, it played a significant role in mobilizing Indian Muslims against British imperialism.
 
• Its decline marked the beginning of communal tensions between Hindus and Muslims in India.
